title: Enhancing Active Learning Performance with Initial Data Selection Based on Foundation Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.24384v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: In active object detection, selecting the initial labeled pool is essential, especially in complex datasets with expensive labeling and low resource budget. This study presents an active learning framework designed to optimize the initial training cycle of active learning for the object detection task. Our approach diverges from traditional methods by utilizing feature-based clustering from the YOLO-World model and refining images based on objectness scores rather than relying on uncertainty sampling in the initial cycle. This approach focuses on finding samples with various features and emphasizes training in areas where the foundation model is most confident. Doing so helps the model better understand different types of objects. For subsequent cycles, we employ a consistency-based sampling technique to maintain the robustness of the training process. To evaluate our method, we use two complex datasets called Aquarium and NWPU VHR-10,

translated_title: 基于基础模型初始数据选择提升主动学习性能
translated_abstract: 在主动目标检测中，选择初始标注池至关重要，尤其是在标注成本高昂、资源预算有限的复杂数据集中。本研究提出了一种主动学习框架，旨在优化目标检测任务中主动学习的初始训练周期。我们的方法与传统方法不同，在初始周期中利用YOLO-World模型进行基于特征的聚类，并根据对象性分数筛选图像，而不是依赖不确定性采样。这种方法侧重于寻找具有多样化特征的样本，并强调在基础模型最有信心的区域进行训练，从而帮助模型更好地理解不同类型的对象。对于后续周期，我们采用基于一致性的采样技术来保持训练过程的稳健性。为了评估我们的方法，我们使用了两个名为Aquarium和NWPU VHR-10的复杂数据集。
tldr: 该论文提出利用YOLO-World基础模型的特征聚类和对象性分数筛选来优化主动学习目标检测的初始数据选择，并在后续周期采用一致性采样，从而在复杂数据集上提升主动学习性能。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an initial data selection approach for active object detection that leverages feature-based clustering and objectness scores from the YOLO-World foundation model to optimize the first training cycle, combined with consistency-based sampling in subsequent cycles to improve active learning performance.
